```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Shared helpers for both simulations on this page ----

// Colors used across widgets (same ink/red/blue palette as Sessions 4-5)
col = ({
  ink: "#33414d", line: "#c9d1d8", muted: "#9aa5ad", soft: "#5f6b75",
  red: "#d1495b", blue: "#1f5f8b", band: "#f6dfe2", series: "#8a98a6"
})

// Seeded random numbers, so "New summer" / "New region" are repeatable and
// the picture doesn't change when only the sampling design changes.
// (mulberry32: a tiny, well-known 32-bit generator.)
rng = seed => {
  let a = seed >>> 0;
  return () => {
    a = (a + 0x6D2B79F5) | 0;
    let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
    t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}

// A standard normal draw (Box-Muller)
rnorm = r => {
  let u = 0;
  while (u === 0) u = r();
  return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * r());
}

// A "New ..." button whose value counts clicks. Built by hand because the
// cosmo theme draws Inputs.button() dark with an invisible label, and
// Quarto's html`` template doesn't attach click handlers (Session 4 note).
counterButton = label => {
  const b = document.createElement("button");
  b.textContent = label;
  b.className = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary";
  b.style.margin = "0.2rem 0 0.6rem";
  // A button's built-in .value is a string ("0" + 1 would give "01"), so
  // replace it with a numeric click counter that OJS reads as the view value
  let clicks = 0;
  Object.defineProperty(b, "value", {get: () => clicks, set: v => { clicks = +v; }});
  b.addEventListener("click", () => {
    clicks += 1;
    b.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
  });
  return b;
}

// The "textbook" 95% CI for a mean: mean ± t * s / sqrt(n).
// This is exactly what lm(y ~ 1) and t.test(y) report. It assumes every
// observation is independent, which is the assumption this page breaks.
naiveCI = (values, tcrit) => {
  const n = values.length;
  const m = d3.mean(values);
  const se = d3.deviation(values) / Math.sqrt(n);
  return {m, se, lo: m - tcrit * se, hi: m + tcrit * se};
}

// Summarize many repeats of the same design.
//   reps: [{err, half, popVar}] where err = estimate - truth,
//   half = CI half-width, popVar = variance over the whole target period/area.
summarize = (reps) => {
  const covered = reps.filter(d => Math.abs(d.err) <= d.half).length / reps.length;
  // Half-width that would really have caught 95% of the truths
  const actual95 = d3.quantile(reps.map(d => Math.abs(d.err)), 0.95);
  const claimed = d3.mean(reps, d => d.half);
  // Effective sample size: how many *randomly placed* readings would give
  // the same typical error (variance of one random reading / mean squared error)
  const mse = d3.mean(reps, d => d.err * d.err);
  const nEff = d3.mean(reps, d => d.popVar) / mse;
  return {covered, actual95, claimed, nEff};
}

// Coverage plot shared by both widgets: one vertical CI per repeat, drawn as
// error (estimate - truth). A bar that crosses the zero line caught the truth.
coveragePlot = (reps, {w, unit, ylim = 4, nShow = 100}) => {
  const h = 210, m = {t: 14, r: 12, b: 30, l: 46};
  const shown = reps.slice(0, nShow);
  const x = d3.scaleLinear().domain([0, shown.length]).range([m.l, w - m.r]);
  const y = d3.scaleLinear().domain([-ylim, ylim]).range([h - m.b, m.t]).clamp(true);
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, w, h]).style("width", "100%").style("max-width", w + "px");
  svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${m.l},0)`)
    .call(d3.axisLeft(y).ticks(5).tickFormat(d => (d > 0 ? "+" : "") + d))
    .call(g => g.selectAll("text").attr("font-size", 11));
  svg.append("text").attr("transform", `translate(12,${(h - m.b + m.t) / 2}) rotate(-90)`)
    .attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", col.soft)
    .text(`estimate − truth (${unit})`);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", (m.l + w - m.r) / 2).attr("y", h - 6).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", col.soft).text(`${shown.length} repeats of the same design`);
  // Zero line = the truth
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", m.l).attr("x2", w - m.r).attr("y1", y(0)).attr("y2", y(0))
    .attr("stroke", col.ink).attr("stroke-dasharray", "4 3");
  const bw = Math.max(1.2, (x(1) - x(0)) * 0.55);
  shown.forEach((d, i) => {
    const hit = Math.abs(d.err) <= d.half;
    const cx = x(i + 0.5);
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", cx).attr("x2", cx)
      .attr("y1", y(d.err - d.half)).attr("y2", y(d.err + d.half))
      .attr("stroke", hit ? col.blue : col.red).attr("stroke-width", bw).attr("stroke-linecap", "round");
    svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx).attr("cy", y(d.err)).attr("r", Math.min(2.2, bw))
      .attr("fill", hit ? col.blue : col.red);
  });
  return svg.node();
}

// The four readout tiles under each coverage plot
readouts = (s, n, unit, what) => {
  const pct = Math.round(100 * s.covered);
  const nEffTxt = s.nEff < 1.5 ? "about 1" : s.nEff >= n ? `${n} or more` : `about ${Math.round(s.nEff)}`;
  return html`<div class="ac-readouts">
    <div><div class="ac-label">95% CIs that caught the truth</div>
      <div class="readout" style="color:${pct >= 90 ? col.blue : col.red}">${pct}%</div></div>
    <div><div class="ac-label">Claimed precision (avg. CI half-width)</div>
      <div class="readout">± ${s.claimed.toFixed(2)} ${unit}</div></div>
    <div><div class="ac-label">Half-width that really catches 95%</div>
      <div class="readout">± ${s.actual95.toFixed(2)} ${unit}</div></div>
    <div><div class="ac-label">Your ${n} ${what} are worth</div>
      <div class="readout">${nEffTxt}</div>
      <div class="ac-label">randomly placed ${what}</div></div>
  </div>`;
}
```

## Today

- Explain **autocorrelation** in time and in space
- Explain why autocorrelated samples produce confidence intervals that are
  **too narrow**
- Tell a sampling design that **adds information** from one that repeats it
- Recognize the fix in R: a model that knows the data are correlated

---

## 1 Near things are more alike

- Tobler's first law: *"Everything is related to everything else, but near
  things are more related than distant things"*
- **In time:** a warm afternoon predicts a warm evening. One hour later, you
  learn almost nothing new
- **In space:** a sensor predicts its neighbor down the street. A second sensor
  there adds little
- This is **autocorrelation**: a variable correlated with *itself* at nearby
  times or places

The usual confidence interval for a mean is

$$\bar{x} \pm t \cdot \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$$

- The $\sqrt{n}$ assumes **each observation brings new, independent
  information**
- `lm()`, `t.test()`, and most AI-written code use this formula by default
- When observations repeat each other, the formula **counts the same
  information many times**

---

## 2 In time: a lake temperature logger

- Goal: the **average surface temperature of a lake this summer**
  (June to August)
- Budget: **20 readings**. You choose how far apart they are
- The lake barely changes from day to night, but it swings with the weather
  over several days

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Predict

You take all 20 readings **one hour apart**. Compared with readings spread over
the whole summer, will the 95% CI be wider or narrower? How often will it
contain the true summer mean?
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Spacing choices. Values are hours between readings; "random" spreads the
// 20 readings at random times over the whole summer.
spacingOpts = new Map([
  ["1 hour", 1], ["6 hours", 6], ["12 hours", 12],
  ["1 day", 24], ["2 days", 48], ["3 days", 72], ["Random times, all summer", "random"]
])
viewof tSpacing = Inputs.radio(spacingOpts, {value: 1, label: "Time between readings"})
viewof tNew = counterButton("New summer")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Temporal model ----
// Hourly lake temperature for 92 days. Weather anomalies follow an AR(1)
// process: each hour keeps most of the previous hour's anomaly.
// tau = 72 h is the "memory" (correlation drops to 37% after 3 days).
T = ({H: 92 * 24, tau: 72, sigma: 1.5, mu: 22, n: 20, tcrit: 2.093})

makeSeries = r => {
  const phi = Math.exp(-1 / T.tau), s = Math.sqrt(1 - phi * phi);
  const x = new Float64Array(T.H);
  let v = rnorm(r) * T.sigma;               // start from the long-run spread
  for (let i = 0; i < T.H; i++) {
    if (i > 0) v = phi * v + s * T.sigma * rnorm(r);
    x[i] = T.mu + v;
  }
  return x;
}

// Hours at which the 20 readings are taken. Evenly spaced readings start at
// a random hour (u in [0, 1)) chosen so the last one still falls in summer.
sampleHours = (u, r, spacing) => {
  if (spacing === "random") {
    const s = new Set();
    while (s.size < T.n) s.add(Math.floor(r() * T.H));
    return [...s].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  }
  const span = (T.n - 1) * spacing;
  const start = Math.floor(u * (T.H - span));
  return d3.range(T.n).map(i => start + i * spacing);
}

// One example summer. The series and the start time use separate seeds, so
// changing the spacing keeps the same summer and roughly the same start.
tExample = {
  const series = makeSeries(rng(100 + tNew));
  const r2 = rng(900 + tNew);
  const hours = sampleHours(r2(), r2, tSpacing);
  const values = hours.map(h => series[h]);
  return {series, hours, values, truth: d3.mean(series), ci: naiveCI(values, T.tcrit)};
}

// 200 more summers with the same design, for the coverage plot
tReps = {
  const r = rng(7 + tNew);
  return d3.range(200).map(() => {
    const series = makeSeries(r);
    const truth = d3.mean(series);
    const values = sampleHours(r(), r, tSpacing).map(h => series[h]);
    const ci = naiveCI(values, T.tcrit);
    return {err: ci.m - truth, half: ci.hi - ci.m, popVar: d3.variance(series)};
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Temporal figure: the summer, the readings, and this sample's CI ----
{
  const w = Math.min(width, 900), h = 260;
  const m = {t: 16, r: 120, b: 30, l: 46};
  const {series, hours, values, truth, ci} = tExample;
  const x = d3.scaleLinear().domain([0, T.H]).range([m.l, w - m.r]);
  const y = d3.scaleLinear().domain([T.mu - 5, T.mu + 5]).range([h - m.b, m.t]).clamp(true);
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, w, h]).style("width", "100%").style("max-width", w + "px");

  // Month axis (day 0 = June 1)
  const months = [["Jun", 0], ["Jul", 30], ["Aug", 61]];
  svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(0,${h - m.b})`)
    .call(d3.axisBottom(x).tickValues(months.map(d => d[1] * 24)).tickFormat((d, i) => months[i][0]))
    .call(g => g.selectAll("text").attr("font-size", 11).attr("text-anchor", "start"));
  svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${m.l},0)`).call(d3.axisLeft(y).ticks(5))
    .call(g => g.selectAll("text").attr("font-size", 11));
  svg.append("text").attr("transform", `translate(12,${(h - m.b + m.t) / 2}) rotate(-90)`)
    .attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", col.soft).text("°C");

  // Shade the stretch of summer the readings cover
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", x(hours[0]) - 2).attr("width", Math.max(4, x(hours.at(-1)) - x(hours[0]) + 4))
    .attr("y", m.t).attr("height", h - m.b - m.t).attr("fill", col.band);

  // The full hourly record (unknown to you in real life)
  const line = d3.line().x((d, i) => x(i)).y(d => y(d));
  svg.append("path").attr("d", line(series)).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", col.series).attr("stroke-width", 1);

  // True summer mean
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", m.l).attr("x2", w - m.r + 40).attr("y1", y(truth)).attr("y2", y(truth))
    .attr("stroke", col.ink).attr("stroke-dasharray", "5 3").attr("stroke-width", 1.5);

  // The 20 readings
  hours.forEach((hr, i) => svg.append("circle").attr("cx", x(hr)).attr("cy", y(values[i]))
    .attr("r", 3.5).attr("fill", col.red).attr("stroke", "white").attr("stroke-width", 0.8));

  // This sample's estimate and 95% CI, in the right margin on the same axis
  const cx = w - m.r + 40, hit = ci.lo <= truth && truth <= ci.hi;
  const c = hit ? col.blue : col.red;
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", cx).attr("x2", cx).attr("y1", y(ci.lo)).attr("y2", y(ci.hi))
    .attr("stroke", c).attr("stroke-width", 4).attr("stroke-linecap", "round");
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx).attr("cy", y(ci.m)).attr("r", 5).attr("fill", c);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", cx + 10).attr("y", y(ci.m) + 4).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", c)
    .text(`${ci.m.toFixed(1)} ± ${(ci.hi - ci.m).toFixed(1)}`);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", cx + 10).attr("y", y(truth) + (ci.m > truth ? 14 : -6)).attr("font-size", 11)
    .attr("fill", col.ink).text(`truth ${truth.toFixed(1)}`);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", cx).attr("y", m.t - 4).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11)
    .attr("fill", col.soft).text("estimate ± CI");

  const s = summarize(tReps);
  return html`<div class="widget">
    ${svg.node()}
    <div class="ac-note">Gray: the lake's full hourly record. Red dots: your 20 readings (shaded: the stretch
      they cover). Dashed: the true summer mean. Right: what <code>lm(temp ~ 1)</code> would report.
      <b>${hit ? "This CI caught the truth." : "This CI missed the truth."}</b></div>
    <h4 class="ac-h">Repeat for 200 summers</h4>
    ${coveragePlot(tReps, {w, unit: "°C"})}
    ${readouts(s, T.n, "°C", "readings")}
  </div>`;
}
```

- Readings an hour apart **all share the same weather**. They agree with each
  other, so $s$ is small and the CI is tiny
- But the whole cluster can sit **far from the summer mean**. The CI misses most
  of the time
- Spreading readings out makes the CI **wider and honest**: wider because it
  finally sees the summer's real variability
- Same $n$, same formula, very different truth

---

## 3 In space: neighborhood heat sensors

- Goal: the **average afternoon air temperature** across a 40 × 40 km region
- Budget: **30 low-cost sensors** hosted by volunteers
- Volunteers tend to live **in the same few neighborhoods**, so sensors cluster

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Predict

All 30 sensors sit inside one 5 km square. Roughly what fraction of
"95%" CIs will contain the region-wide mean: 95%, 50%, or 10%?
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof sSize = Inputs.range([1, 40], {value: 5, step: 1, label: "Width of the sensor cluster (km)"})
viewof sNew = counterButton("New region")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Spatial model ----
// A smooth random temperature surface built from M random waves
// (random Fourier features). Waves with random directions and wavelengths
// give a surface whose correlation fades with distance; ell = 5 km sets how
// fast (correlation drops to about 60% at 5 km and 14% at 10 km).
S = ({L: 40, ell: 5, M: 200, sigma: 1.5, mu: 31, n: 30, tcrit: 2.045})

makeField = r => d3.range(S.M).map(() => [rnorm(r) / S.ell, rnorm(r) / S.ell, r() * 2 * Math.PI])
fieldAt = (f, x, y) => {
  let s = 0;
  for (const [a, b, p] of f) s += Math.cos(a * x + b * y + p);
  return S.mu + S.sigma * Math.sqrt(2 / S.M) * s;
}

// Exact region-wide mean of the surface (the "truth"): each wave's integral
// over the square has a closed form, so no grid approximation is needed.
fieldMean = f => {
  const L = S.L;
  const I = a => Math.abs(a) < 1e-9 ? [L, 0] : [Math.sin(a * L) / a, (1 - Math.cos(a * L)) / a];
  let s = 0;
  for (const [a, b, p] of f) {
    const [ar, ai] = I(a), [br, bi] = I(b);
    const pr = ar * br - ai * bi, pi = ar * bi + ai * br;   // complex product
    s += Math.cos(p) * pr - Math.sin(p) * pi;               // real part of e^{ip} * product
  }
  return S.mu + S.sigma * Math.sqrt(2 / S.M) * s / (L * L);
}

// Keep a cluster of width c fully inside the region
clampCenter = (v, c) => Math.max(c / 2, Math.min(S.L - c / 2, v))

// 30 sensors scattered uniformly inside a c x c square centered on (cx, cy)
placeSensors = (r, cx, cy, c) => d3.range(S.n).map(() => [cx + (r() - 0.5) * c, cy + (r() - 0.5) * c])

// Where the example cluster sits. Clicking the map moves it.
mutable sCenter = [12, 26]

sExample = {
  const f = makeField(rng(300 + sNew));
  const cx = clampCenter(sCenter[0], sSize), cy = clampCenter(sCenter[1], sSize);
  const pts = placeSensors(rng(500), cx, cy, sSize);
  const values = pts.map(([x, y]) => fieldAt(f, x, y));
  return {f, cx, cy, pts, values, truth: fieldMean(f), ci: naiveCI(values, S.tcrit)};
}

// The example surface on an 80 x 80 grid, for drawing the map
sGrid = {
  const g = 80, vals = new Float64Array(g * g);
  for (let j = 0; j < g; j++)
    for (let i = 0; i < g; i++)
      vals[j * g + i] = fieldAt(sExample.f, (i + 0.5) * S.L / g, S.L - (j + 0.5) * S.L / g);
  return {g, vals};
}

// 200 more regions, each with the cluster dropped at a random spot
sReps = {
  const r = rng(11 + sNew);
  return d3.range(200).map(() => {
    const f = makeField(r);
    const truth = fieldMean(f);
    const cx = sSize / 2 + r() * (S.L - sSize), cy = sSize / 2 + r() * (S.L - sSize);
    const values = placeSensors(r, cx, cy, sSize).map(([x, y]) => fieldAt(f, x, y));
    const ci = naiveCI(values, S.tcrit);
    // Spread of one random point in the region, from a coarse 12 x 12 grid
    const grid = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) for (let j = 0; j < 12; j++) grid.push(fieldAt(f, (i + 0.5) * S.L / 12, (j + 0.5) * S.L / 12));
    return {err: ci.m - truth, half: ci.hi - ci.m, popVar: d3.variance(grid)};
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Spatial figure: the surface, the sensors, and this sample's CI ----
{
  const wide = width > 640;
  const mapW = wide ? 360 : Math.min(width - 10, 360);
  const {cx, cy, pts, values, truth, ci} = sExample;
  const color = d3.scaleSequential(d3.interpolateRdYlBu).domain([S.mu + 3.5, S.mu - 3.5]);

  // Paint the grid into a small canvas, then show it scaled up (smoothly)
  const {g, vals} = sGrid;
  const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
  canvas.width = g; canvas.height = g;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d"), img = ctx.createImageData(g, g);
  vals.forEach((v, k) => {
    const c = d3.rgb(color(v));
    img.data.set([c.r, c.g, c.b, 255], k * 4);
  });
  ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);

  const k = mapW / S.L;   // pixels per km
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, mapW, mapW]).style("width", mapW + "px")
    .style("cursor", "crosshair");
  svg.append("image").attr("href", canvas.toDataURL()).attr("width", mapW).attr("height", mapW)
    .attr("preserveAspectRatio", "none");
  svg.append("rect").attr("width", mapW).attr("height", mapW).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", col.ink);
  // Cluster outline and sensors (map y runs up, SVG y runs down)
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", (cx - sSize / 2) * k).attr("y", (S.L - cy - sSize / 2) * k)
    .attr("width", sSize * k).attr("height", sSize * k)
    .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", col.ink).attr("stroke-dasharray", "4 3");
  pts.forEach(([x, y]) => svg.append("circle").attr("cx", x * k).attr("cy", (S.L - y) * k)
    .attr("r", 3.2).attr("fill", "white").attr("stroke", col.ink).attr("stroke-width", 1.2));
  // 10 km scale bar
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", 8).attr("y", mapW - 16).attr("width", 10 * k).attr("height", 5).attr("fill", col.ink);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 8).attr("y", mapW - 20).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", col.ink).text("10 km");
  // Click to move the cluster
  svg.on("click", (event) => {
    const [px, py] = d3.pointer(event);
    mutable sCenter = [px / k, S.L - py / k];
  });

  // ---- CI strip on a temperature axis, with a color legend ----
  const sh = mapW, sw = 170, m = {t: 16, b: 16};
  const y = d3.scaleLinear().domain([S.mu - 3.5, S.mu + 3.5]).range([sh - m.b, m.t]).clamp(true);
  const strip = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, sw, sh]).style("width", sw + "px");
  const ramp = d3.range(0, 1.001, 0.05);
  const grad = strip.append("defs").append("linearGradient").attr("id", "ac-ramp")
    .attr("x1", 0).attr("x2", 0).attr("y1", 1).attr("y2", 0);
  ramp.forEach(t => grad.append("stop").attr("offset", t).attr("stop-color", color(S.mu - 3.5 + 7 * t)));
  strip.append("rect").attr("x", 30).attr("y", m.t).attr("width", 10).attr("height", sh - m.t - m.b).attr("fill", "url(#ac-ramp)");
  strip.append("g").attr("transform", "translate(30,0)").call(d3.axisLeft(y).ticks(6))
    .call(g => g.selectAll("text").attr("font-size", 11));
  strip.append("text").attr("x", 2).attr("y", 10).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", col.soft).text("°C");
  const hit = ci.lo <= truth && truth <= ci.hi, c = hit ? col.blue : col.red, bx = 70;
  strip.append("line").attr("x1", 44).attr("x2", sw - 4).attr("y1", y(truth)).attr("y2", y(truth))
    .attr("stroke", col.ink).attr("stroke-dasharray", "5 3").attr("stroke-width", 1.5);
  strip.append("line").attr("x1", bx).attr("x2", bx).attr("y1", y(ci.lo)).attr("y2", y(ci.hi))
    .attr("stroke", c).attr("stroke-width", 4).attr("stroke-linecap", "round");
  strip.append("circle").attr("cx", bx).attr("cy", y(ci.m)).attr("r", 5).attr("fill", c);
  strip.append("text").attr("x", bx + 10).attr("y", y(ci.m) + 4).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", c)
    .text(`${ci.m.toFixed(1)} ± ${(ci.hi - ci.m).toFixed(1)}`);
  strip.append("text").attr("x", bx + 10).attr("y", y(truth) + (ci.m > truth ? 14 : -6)).attr("font-size", 11)
    .attr("fill", col.ink).text(`truth ${truth.toFixed(1)}`);

  const s = summarize(sReps);
  const cw = Math.min(width, 900);
  return html`<div class="widget">
    <div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:1rem;align-items:flex-start">
      <div>${svg.node()}</div>
      <div>${strip.node()}</div>
    </div>
    <div class="ac-note">Colors: the true temperature surface (unknown to you in real life). White dots:
      your 30 sensors. <b>Click the map to move the cluster.</b> Right: what <code>lm(temp ~ 1)</code>
      would report, against the true region-wide mean (dashed).
      <b>${hit ? "This CI caught the truth." : "This CI missed the truth."}</b></div>
    <h4 class="ac-h">Repeat for 200 regions (cluster dropped at a random spot each time)</h4>
    ${coveragePlot(sReps, {w: cw, unit: "°C"})}
    ${readouts(s, S.n, "°C", "sensors")}
  </div>`;
}
```

- Same story as the lake: clustered sensors **agree with each other**, so the CI
  is narrow, but they describe **one neighborhood**, not the region
- Misses go **both ways** (too hot and too cold). Clustering doesn't bias the
  estimate on average. It makes it **far less precise than claimed**
- Once the cluster is wider than the correlation distance (about 10 km here),
  the sensors start adding real information

---

## 4 Why it happens: effective sample size

Two things go wrong at once:

1. **The $\sqrt{n}$ is too generous.** Correlated observations overlap in what
   they tell you. The *effective* sample size $n_\text{eff}$ is smaller than $n$
2. **$s$ is too small.** Clustered points see only a slice of the variability
   (the red dots cover a sliver of the lake's range)

For readings in a time series where each one correlates $\rho$ with the next
(an AR(1) process), a common approximation is

$$n_\text{eff} \approx n \, \frac{1 - \rho}{1 + \rho}$$

| Correlation between neighbors ($\rho$) | 20 readings are worth about |
|---|---|
| 0 | 20 |
| 0.5 | 7 |
| 0.8 | 2 |
| 0.99 (one hour apart in the lake) | about 1 |

- The "worth about" tile in each widget estimates the same idea from the
  simulations
- Evenly spaced readings over the whole summer can do **better than random**,
  because they never bunch up (try "3 days" vs. "Random times" in the lake
  widget)

---

## 5 In R: a model that knows about the correlation

`lm()` assumes independent errors. `nlme::gls()` (generalized least squares)
fits the same mean but also **estimates how the errors are correlated** and
widens the CI to match.

### In time

```{r}
#| label: libraries
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(nlme)   # gls() and correlation structures; ships with R
library(MASS)   # mvrnorm(), to simulate a correlated surface; ships with R
```

```{r}
#| label: ci-table
# Small helper: one row per model with the estimate, the 95% CI, and the
# CI's width, so the two models are easy to compare at a glance
ci_table <- function(...) {
  models <- list(...)
  rows <- lapply(models, function(m) {
    ci <- confint(m)[1, ]
    c(estimate = unname(coef(m)[1]), lower = unname(ci[1]),
      upper = unname(ci[2]), width = unname(ci[2] - ci[1]))
  })
  round(do.call(rbind, rows), 2)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: lake-sim
# Simulate 60 daily lake readings with day-to-day correlation 0.7.
# The true long-run mean is 22 °C.
set.seed(42)
n_days <- 60
temp <- 22 + as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.7), n = n_days,
                                  sd = 1.5 * sqrt(1 - 0.7^2)))
lake <- data.frame(day = 1:n_days, temp = temp)
```

```{r}
#| label: lake-acf
#| fig-height: 3.5
# Diagnose first: the autocorrelation function (ACF).
# Bars beyond the blue dashed lines = correlation at that lag.
acf(lake$temp, main = "Lake temperature: autocorrelation by lag (days)")
```

```{r}
#| label: lake-models
# Naive: assumes the 60 days are independent
m_lm <- lm(temp ~ 1, data = lake)

# Aware: each day's error is correlated with the previous day's (AR(1))
m_gls <- gls(temp ~ 1, data = lake, correlation = corAR1(form = ~ day))

# The two models side by side
ci_table(lm = m_lm, gls = m_gls)
```

- Nearly the same estimate (`gls()` gives less weight to runs of correlated
  days), but compare the `width` column: the `gls()` CI is about **three
  times wider**
- `gls()` estimated the day-to-day correlation itself (printed as `Phi` in
  `summary(m_gls)`)

### In space

```{r}
#| label: sensor-sim
# Simulate 80 sensors in 4 clustered neighborhoods of a 40 x 40 km region.
# Temperatures are correlated with distance (exponential, range 6 km).
# The true mean is 31 °C.
set.seed(7)
n <- 80
centers <- cbind(runif(4, 5, 35), runif(4, 5, 35))
xy <- centers[rep(1:4, each = 20), ] + matrix(rnorm(2 * n, sd = 1.5), ncol = 2)
Sigma <- 1.5^2 * exp(-as.matrix(dist(xy)) / 6)   # covariance by distance
sensors <- data.frame(x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2],
                      temp = 31 + mvrnorm(1, rep(0, n), Sigma))
```

```{r}
#| label: sensor-models
# Naive
s_lm <- lm(temp ~ 1, data = sensors)

# Aware: errors correlated by distance (exponential decay with x-y distance)
s_gls <- gls(temp ~ 1, data = sensors, correlation = corExp(form = ~ x + y))

# The two models side by side
ci_table(lm = s_lm, gls = s_gls)
```

- The `lm()` CI **misses 31**. The `gls()` CI, more than four times wider,
  contains it
- `corExp(form = ~ x + y)` needs **projected** coordinates (meters or km), not
  degrees (Session 4)
- Tools for *measuring* spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I, variograms) come in
  a later session

---

## 6 Closing the loop: naive vs. honest CIs

- Repeat the lake example **200 times** at each strength of day-to-day
  correlation ($\rho$), from none to strong
- Fit **both** models every time, and check whether each 95% CI contains the
  true long-run mean (22 °C)

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Predict

With no autocorrelation ($\rho = 0$), which model's CIs will be wider? What
happens to each model's CIs as $\rho$ grows?
:::

```{r}
#| label: gls-sim
# Simulate the lake many times at several strengths of autocorrelation, and
# fit lm() and gls() to every simulated summer. (This takes ~15 s; freeze
# saves the result, so it only re-runs when this page's source changes.)
set.seed(2027)
rhos   <- c(0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.8, 0.9)   # day-to-day correlation
n_days <- 60                         # readings per summer
n_reps <- 200                        # simulated summers per rho
mu     <- 22                         # true long-run mean (°C)

sim_rows <- list()
for (rho in rhos) {
  for (k in 1:n_reps) {
    # AR(1) series with a total SD of 1.5 °C, whatever rho is
    temp <- if (rho == 0) {
      rnorm(n_days, mu, 1.5)
    } else {
      mu + as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = rho), n = n_days,
                                sd = 1.5 * sqrt(1 - rho^2)))
    }
    d <- data.frame(day = 1:n_days, temp = temp)

    # The two models from above
    fits <- list(
      lm  = lm(temp ~ 1, data = d),
      gls = tryCatch(gls(temp ~ 1, data = d, correlation = corAR1(form = ~ day)),
                     error = function(e) NULL)   # skip a rare failed fit
    )
    for (model in names(fits)) {
      if (is.null(fits[[model]])) next
      ci <- confint(fits[[model]])[1, ]
      sim_rows[[length(sim_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        rho = rho, rep = k, model = model,
        est = unname(coef(fits[[model]])[1]), lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2])
    }
  }
}
sim <- do.call(rbind, sim_rows)

# Coverage (share of CIs containing mu) and median CI width, by model and rho.
# Median, not mean: at strong rho a few gls() fits give huge CIs (see below).
sim$covered <- sim$lo <= mu & sim$hi >= mu
sim$width   <- sim$hi - sim$lo
coverage <- merge(
  aggregate(covered ~ model + rho, data = sim, FUN = mean),
  aggregate(width ~ model + rho, data = sim, FUN = median))
coverage$width <- round(coverage$width, 2)
coverage[order(coverage$rho, coverage$model), ]

# Hand the simulations to the interactive figure below
ojs_define(glsSim = sim)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof rhoPick = Inputs.radio(
  new Map([["0 (independent)", 0], ["0.3", 0.3], ["0.6", 0.6], ["0.8", 0.8], ["0.9 (strong)", 0.9]]),
  {value: 0.8, label: "Day-to-day correlation (ρ)"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Naive vs. honest CIs, from the R simulation above ----
{
  // ojs_define() hands over a data frame as columns; transpose() makes rows
  const sim = transpose(glsSim).map(d => ({...d, err: d.est - 22, half: (d.hi - d.lo) / 2}));
  const models = [
    {key: "lm", label: "assumes independence", color: col.red},
    {key: "gls", label: "models the correlation", color: col.blue}
  ];

  // Summary by model and rho: coverage and median CI width
  const rhos = [...new Set(sim.map(d => d.rho))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const stats = models.map(mo => ({...mo, pts: rhos.map(r => {
    const s = sim.filter(d => d.model === mo.key && d.rho === r);
    return {rho: r, cover: s.filter(d => Math.abs(d.err) <= d.half).length / s.length,
            width: d3.median(s, d => d.hi - d.lo)};
  })}));

  // ---- Top: coverage vs. rho, one line per model ----
  const w = Math.min(width, 900), h = 220, m = {t: 16, r: 110, b: 36, l: 50};
  const x = d3.scaleLinear().domain([0, 0.9]).range([m.l, w - m.r]);
  const y = d3.scaleLinear().domain([0.2, 1]).range([h - m.b, m.t]);
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, w, h]).style("width", "100%").style("max-width", w + "px");
  // Highlight the chosen rho (drawn first so it sits behind the lines)
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", x(rhoPick)).attr("x2", x(rhoPick)).attr("y1", m.t).attr("y2", h - m.b)
    .attr("stroke", col.line).attr("stroke-width", 10).attr("opacity", 0.6);
  svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(0,${h - m.b})`).call(d3.axisBottom(x).tickValues(rhos))
    .call(g => g.selectAll("text").attr("font-size", 11));
  svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${m.l},0)`).call(d3.axisLeft(y).ticks(5, "%"))
    .call(g => g.selectAll("text").attr("font-size", 11));
  svg.append("text").attr("x", (m.l + w - m.r) / 2).attr("y", h - 4).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", col.soft).text("day-to-day correlation (ρ)");
  svg.append("text").attr("transform", `translate(12,${(h - m.b + m.t) / 2}) rotate(-90)`)
    .attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", col.soft).text("CIs that caught the truth");
  // The promise: 95%
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", m.l).attr("x2", w - m.r).attr("y1", y(0.95)).attr("y2", y(0.95))
    .attr("stroke", col.ink).attr("stroke-dasharray", "4 3");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", w - m.r + 8).attr("y", y(0.95) + 4).attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", col.ink)
    .text("promised 95%");
  for (const s of stats) {
    svg.append("path").attr("d", d3.line().x(d => x(d.rho)).y(d => y(d.cover))(s.pts))
      .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", s.color).attr("stroke-width", 2.5);
    s.pts.forEach(d => svg.append("circle").attr("cx", x(d.rho)).attr("cy", y(d.cover))
      .attr("r", d.rho === rhoPick ? 6 : 4).attr("fill", s.color));
    const last = s.pts.at(-1);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", x(last.rho) + 10).attr("y", y(last.cover) + 4).attr("font-size", 12)
      .attr("font-weight", 600).attr("fill", s.color).text(s.key + "()");
  }

  // ---- Bottom: the first 100 CIs at the chosen rho, one plot per model ----
  const wide = width > 640;
  const pw = wide ? (w - 24) / 2 : w;
  const panels = stats.map(s => {
    const reps = sim.filter(d => d.model === s.key && d.rho === rhoPick);
    const p = s.pts.find(d => d.rho === rhoPick);
    return html`<div>
      <div style="font-weight:600;color:${s.color};margin-bottom:.2rem"><code>${s.key}()</code>: ${s.label}</div>
      ${coveragePlot(reps, {w: pw, unit: "°C", ylim: 3})}
      <div class="ac-readouts">
        <div><div class="ac-label">CIs that caught the truth</div>
          <div class="readout" style="color:${p.cover >= 0.9 ? col.blue : col.red}">${Math.round(100 * p.cover)}%</div></div>
        <div><div class="ac-label">Median CI width</div>
          <div class="readout">${p.width.toFixed(2)} °C</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>`;
  });

  return html`<div class="widget">
    ${svg.node()}
    <div class="ac-note">Each point summarizes 200 simulated summers of 60 daily readings. The gray band marks
      the ρ chosen above, shown in detail below. (Bar colors below: blue caught the truth, red missed.)</div>
    <div style="display:${wide ? "grid" : "block"};grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:24px;margin-top:1rem">
      ${panels}
    </div>
  </div>`;
}
```

- With **no autocorrelation**, the two models agree: same widths, about 95%
  coverage. `gls()` costs little when it isn't needed
- As $\rho$ grows, `lm()` keeps reporting **a narrow CI** (it even shrinks a
  little) while its coverage collapses
- `gls()` **widens its CIs to match** and stays much closer to 95%
- Not perfect: with 60 readings, `gls()` must *estimate* $\rho$ too, so it falls
  a bit short at strong correlation (and now and then gives a huge CI when it
  can't tell the mean from a slow drift). Good sampling design still beats any
  model fix

---

## 7 In your code

| Question | Function | What to look for |
|---|---|---|
| Are my observations correlated in time? | `acf(resid(model))` | Bars past the blue lines at lag 1, 2, ... |
| ...in space? | Moran's I, variogram (later session) | Similar values near each other |
| Fit a mean or trend that allows for it (time) | `gls(y ~ x, correlation = corAR1(form = ~ t))` | A wider, more honest CI |
| ...(space) | `gls(y ~ x, correlation = corExp(form = ~ x + y))` | Same; coordinates must be projected |
| Avoid it by design | Spread samples out in time and space | Gaps longer than the correlation distance |

- **AI check:** when AI code reports a CI or p-value from `lm()` on a time
  series or on clustered points, ask: *are these observations independent?*
- Autocorrelation rarely produces errors. It produces **confident wrong answers**

## 8 Check yourself

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 1. One air-quality monitor logs PM2.5 every hour for a year (8,760 readings). `t.test()` gives a mean of 9.1 ± 0.04 µg/m³. Is ± 0.04 believable?

- No. Hourly readings from one monitor are strongly autocorrelated: pollution
  episodes last days
- The effective sample size is far below 8,760, so the true uncertainty about
  the annual mean is much larger
- Check with `acf()`; fit with `gls(..., correlation = corAR1())`, or average
  to daily or weekly values first and check those too
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 2. You can afford 50 soil samples to estimate county-wide soil carbon. Design A: 50 samples in one farm. Design B: one sample in each of 50 farms across the county. Which CI can you trust?

- **B.** Its samples are far apart, so they're close to independent and
  represent the whole county
- A's samples describe one farm. Its CI will be narrow and, for the county, very
  likely wrong (like the 5 km sensor cluster)
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 3. Does autocorrelation make the estimate itself wrong, or only its CI?

- Mostly the **CI**. In both widgets, the misses scatter above *and* below the
  truth, so the estimate isn't biased on average
- But any *one* clustered estimate can be far off, and the narrow CI hides that
- If the clusters are placed non-randomly (e.g., volunteers only in cool, leafy
  neighborhoods), you get **bias** on top of overconfidence
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 4. An AI fits `lm(temp ~ year)` to 40 years of monthly temperatures and reports a warming trend with p < 0.001. What do you ask before believing the p-value?

- Are the residuals autocorrelated? Check `acf(resid(model))`
- If yes, refit with `gls(temp ~ year, correlation = corAR1())` and compare
- The trend may still be real, but the p-value from `lm()` overstates the
  evidence, for the same reason the CIs above were too narrow
:::

  in the analysis of species distributional data: a review. *Ecography*, 30(5),
  609–628.
